groups.sentence: AI governance bodies are appointed with set membership, including faculty, student and unit representatives.
Designated offices develop guidance, policies and protocols on AI use.
Institutions establish or appoint a standing AI committee, council or executive authority with defined authority.
Units designate AI leads, ambassadors or defined roles to coordinate AI work.
Instructors review or discuss their AI policy with their dean, chair or program director.
Instructors get prior written approval from the program director before setting an individual course AI policy.
Students get instructor approval for accommodations or exceptions to course AI rules and contact the instructor to discuss them.
Denials, disputes and unresolved questions are escalated to a named committee, leader or program head.
Academic misconduct involving AI is handled by the conduct office or instructor, who determine violations.
A named body reviews, updates and maintains the AI policy and guidelines over time.
Designated offices review and audit campus procedures and AI use to monitor compliance.
Final authority to interpret the AI policy and decide on it rests with the president or governing board.
AI committees and councils provide oversight, strategy, advice, risk review and policy guidance.
IT, security or compliance offices are responsible for implementing and enforcing the AI policy.
The provost or academic affairs office is responsible for academic AI policy and standards.
Leaders and units ensure their teams understand, implement and comply with the AI policy.
Exceptions to the AI policy are approved by a designated office or committee through a defined request process.
A named office reviews and approves AI tools and maintains the list of approved tools.
